name: Number One & FB Logistics
description1: Number One and FB Logistics are two brands of the same group. FB Logistics is the transport company, specialised in express and custom transport in Belgium and Europe, and Number One is the group’s express delivery brand, which is why its website says “From the FB Logistics Group” under the logo. I joined as the first member of the newly created IT and digitalization department, and my job was to give both brands a proper digital presence and practical tools for the team and for customers. I also took the photos of the fleet and the loading docks shown here.
description2: The main deliverable was the Number One website, built for mobile and desktop with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. It is available in French, Dutch and English and presents the services, the process (reception, preparation, delivery), the fleet and the company, with a clear Get a Quote button. Next to it I built a single page that presents both companies together: FB Logistics and Number One in tabs, the full fleet with weight, volume and pallet capacity per vehicle, the type of cargo each one can carry (box, baché, frigo, pharma, general cargo, ADR), certifications and contact details, in three languages. I also built the quote calculator, a five-step flow that takes a customer from the shipment and cargo details to a price estimate.
description3: The calculator recommends a vehicle for the cargo and lets the user change it, and each vehicle opens a detail view with its interior dimensions, useful volume and payload. Pricing works in several modes (shuttle, route and hourly), covers extras such as waiting time, extra stops and night surcharges, applies a fuel surcharge, and the quote can be printed or downloaded. Beyond the web, I tested two ideas for the daily work of the team: an email automation system built with Node.js, the Gmail API and the Claude API, with a validation layer that checks that the information is complete, and a prototype of a driver management app. Both were tests, and the next step was to take them from test to daily use. In the end the group had a new digital presence for both brands, photos of its real fleet, a quote calculator and two working prototypes to build on.

name: EHB Arcade
description1: The challenge was to design and build a fully functional arcade machine that combined physical craftsmanship, electronics, and software development. The goal was to create a visually appealing, ergonomic, and interactive gaming experience that could engage users while demonstrating seamless integration of hardware and software. Key obstacles included coordinating the electronics with the game software, optimizing the control layout, and ensuring the cabinet was both durable and inviting.
description2: To inform the design, I studied classic arcade machines to understand their proportions, button layouts, and aesthetic appeal. I evaluated various game engines and chose Godot for its flexibility and suitability for 2D game development. On the hardware side, I explored joystick and button configurations, testing wiring and input methods to ensure reliable communication between the controls and the game engine. This research guided both the physical construction and the software integration of the project.
description3: The EHB Arcade was successfully built as a working arcade machine with a custom-designed game. The joystick and buttons responded accurately, providing an intuitive and engaging gameplay experience. While there were minor imperfections in the paint finish and the game mechanics could be further refined, the prototype met its primary objectives. This project demonstrates my ability to merge design, electronics, and software development into a cohesive interactive product, delivering both functionality and entertainment.

name: Eregum
description1: A branding project where I set out to invent a fictional chewing gum brand from scratch, covering the name, concept, logo, packaging, and promotional materials. After evaluating several directions, I committed to the most provocative one: EREGUM, a gum designed to improve sexual performance, directly inspired by Viagra. The bold concept cut through the noise and gave every design decision a clear, consistent direction.
description2: With the concept established, I designed a logo that was both eye-catching and aligned with the product's theme. Next, I created packaging inspired by condom boxes, with the gum placed in “condom-like” bags containing ten pieces each. This approach reinforced the theme while making the product feel fun and unique. Finally, I produced promotional materials, including posters and Instagram visuals. I focused on creating a cohesive brand identity, ensuring that the messaging and aesthetics were consistent across all platforms.
description3: The project concluded successfully. The strong concept, creative packaging, and thoughtfully executed promotional materials made EREGUM stand out. Even as a fictional product, it came across as a complete and cohesive brand.

name: Hiking Gileppe
description1: Aire de Bivouac de la Gileppe. A lively group hike with friends through the lush forests near La Gileppe. Stunning landscapes, vibrant greenery, and plenty of laughs along the way — the perfect mix of adventure and good company.

name: Hiking Hernoy
description1: Bivouac du Bois d'Hernoy. A peaceful escape into the woods — I hiked with a friend to the Bivouac du Bois d'Hernoy and captured the calm, intimate vibe of the trail. A quiet adventure full of nature’s small details.

name: World Without Bees
description1: This project was created to make people aware of the crucial role bees play in our ecosystems and food systems. Bees are among the most important pollinators, responsible for pollinating around 70 of the 100 crop species that feed 90% of the world’s population. Without them, biodiversity, food availability, and entire ecosystems would collapse.
description2: The goal of the installation is to give users an interactive experience of what could happen if bees disappeared. By removing bees from a cardboard beehive, the landscape shown on a screen slowly becomes more empty, grey, and lifeless. Placing the bees back restores the environment, making it greener and more lively again.
description3: Although the interaction is simple, the project carries a deep message about environmental fragility and the importance of pollinators.

name: SPARX
description1: Solo boxers often train without feedback, making it hard to improve accuracy, timing, and rhythm. Most smart punching bags depend on cloud services or subscriptions, which adds cost, latency, and friction.
description2: SPARX was developed using Velostat pressure sensors, an ESP32 microcontroller, and a locally hosted Node.js + React interface. The system was iterated through sensor calibration, punch-detection tuning, and UI testing to ensure reliable, real-time feedback.
description3: SPARX turns any punching bag into a coach-like training partner with live metrics, interactive drills, and mini-games. It works fully offline over local Wi-Fi, offering a fast, affordable, and plug-and-play solution for effective solo training.

name: STAR
description1: STAR is a raw expression of ambition. Born from sketchbooks and late-night ideas, shaped by Tokyo energy. For those who move different.
description2: STAR isn't just clothing — it's direction. A symbol for those building in silence and shining on purpose. From paper concepts to real-world presence.
description3: Every STAR piece carries a mindset. Discipline. Growth. Individuality. Not made to fit in — made to stand out. My role covered the full creative process: brand identity, logo design, apparel graphics, lookbook layout, and the motion content used across social.

name: SOLDIAS
description1: SOLDIAS is not a brand. It's a code. Built on endurance, loyalty, and growth. For those who choose discipline over comfort.
description2: SOLDIAS stands for the ones who keep going. Through pressure. Through doubt. Through silence. We don't follow trends. We build character.
description3: SOLDIAS is for the disciplined dreamers. The quiet grinders. The ones who carry weight and never fold. Strength is earned. Loyalty is lived. I handled the complete brand build: visual identity, typography system, and the website — designed and deployed as a standalone React app.

name: Be My Valentine
description1: A playful interactive Valentine web app where the “No” button can't win — every time it's hovered or clicked, the “Yes” button grows bigger until she finally gives in, triggering a sweet animated surprise and a “Yay 💖” moment.

name: Roast And Ritual
description1: A modern website for a local coffee shop, designed to capture warmth, authenticity, and community. Showcasing the menu, story, location, and contact details in a clean, inviting layout that feels just like stepping into the café itself.
description2: A sleek, responsive website crafted for an independent coffee brand. Built to highlight signature drinks, atmosphere, and identity — turning online visitors into loyal customers through strong visuals and clear storytelling.

name: The Accumulation Room
description1: An experimental interactive art gallery where the screen gradually fills with artworks as the user scrolls. Hidden interactions and easter eggs invite exploration as the space becomes increasingly dense and visually chaotic.
description2: At the end of the experience, the visitor is asked whether they want to clear the gallery. If they choose to do so, everything disappears, revealing the message: “Kill your darlings.” — a reflection on creativity and the importance of letting go of ideas to make space for better ones.

name: The Internet Museum of Forgotten Ideas
description1: An experimental interactive website designed as a fictional digital museum showcasing inventions that humanity almost built but ultimately abandoned. As visitors scroll through the gallery, they discover different exhibits—each presenting a forgotten idea with its own small interactive experiment.
description2: Every artifact invites the user to explore and imagine what these inventions could have become, blending storytelling with playful interaction. The experience ends with an empty pedestal labeled “Your Idea,” reminding visitors that every forgotten innovation once began as a simple thought.

name: The Infinite Corridor
description1: An experimental interactive experience where the user explores an endless corridor filled with mysterious doors. As visitors move forward, each door opens into a small surreal micro-world, creating a sense of curiosity and discovery.
description2: Each room introduces a different interactive environment—distorting gravity, playing with light, or transforming the cursor—gradually turning the corridor into a dreamlike journey. At the end, the user discovers that the entire path forms a hidden labyrinth, revealing the message: “Curiosity builds the labyrinth.”
